title: Test player-versus-player rules with a stand-in when only one client exists
observation: A single-client Studio session cannot create a second Player. The catch, knockdown, immunity and close-range steal rules were still exercised on the server with the real goblin as victim and a stand-in table (a rig plus the few Player members the code uses) as the thief. It found the order and timing mistakes in the test, refused a steal on a standing target, a steal from too far, and a catch inside a protected zone.
recommendation: Write server rules so they take the player objects as arguments, then drive them from a temporary test hook with a stand-in. State plainly in the report that replication, latency, prompts and real input were not covered.
applies_when: Adding a rule between two players
Only one client is available to test with
limits: A stand-in does not test replication, latency, client prompts or real input
A real two-client or multi-client session is still required before calling the feature multiplayer-ready

evidence.detail: Section 10 lists the stand-in thief tests and what they did not cover.
